_comment: Maps Adobe Camera Raw / Lightroom XMP crs: attributes to darktable module slider actions. 'path' is the darktable Lua gui.action path (module/slider). 'verified' true means confirmed against darktable 5.6.0's own Lua examples/docs; false means best-guess, will be logged if it fails so you can correct it via Preferences > Shortcuts search in darktable, then edit this file. 'scale' converts the ACR numeric value into whatever unit darktable's slider expects (a * value + b). 'enable_module' is the iop path to enable (dt.gui.action(path, 'enable', '', '') if not already on).

entries.note: ACR Exposure2012 is already in EV stops, same unit as darktable exposure slider.

Confirmed working 2026-08-23: dt.gui.action returned a real (non-nan) value and the module landed enabled in the history stack. Exact -100..100 range mapping to velvia's scale not independently verified, just that the path resolves.
Confirmed working 2026-08-23: dt.gui.action returned a real (non-nan) value and the module landed enabled in the history stack.
Internal op name is 'hazeremoval' (confirmed via libhazeremoval.so); base module path fixed 2026-08-23, sub-widget name still unverified.

darktable's 'local contrast' UI module is internally named 'bilat' (there is no liblocalcontrast.so) -- fixed the base module path 2026-08-23, sub-widget name still unverified. Not a 1:1 algorithm match with ACR Clarity regardless.

colorzones_note: HueAdjustment* / SaturationAdjustment* / LuminanceAdjustment* (Red/Orange/Yellow/Green/Aqua/Blue/Purple/Magenta) are handled in code (xmp_to_darktable.py: COLORZONES_GROUPS / colorzones_node_actions), not via this entries table, because each needs a curve-tab switch plus two sequential dt.gui.action calls (force-to-floor, then land-on-target) rather than a single value/set. SOLVED 2026-08-23: the curve-tab widget is named 'channel', not 'page' -- found by reading darktable's actual C source (src/iop/colorzones.c: dt_action_define_iop(self, NULL, N_('channel'), GTK_WIDGET(g->channel_tabs), ...)), which also revealed the three page names are 'lightness', 'chroma', 'hue' (NOT 'saturation', which is why every earlier name-guess against a 'page' widget failed). dt.gui.action('iop/colorzones/channel', <tab>, 'activate', 1.0) switches tabs; confirmed by testing directly that all three tabs share identical calibration: dt.gui.action('iop/colorzones/graph', <channel>, 'down'/'up', speed) is linear, each unit of speed moves the node by 0.01, floor=2.0, neutral=2.5, ceiling=3.0, on every tab.
shadhi_blend_note: Highlights2012/Shadows2012/ParametricShadows/ParametricDarks/ParametricLights/ParametricHighlights are all handled together in code (xmp_to_darktable.py: shadhi_blend_actions), not via this entries table, because they're combined into shadhi's same two sliders rather than each getting its own action. This exists because darktable has no widget shaped like ACR's 4-zone parametric tone curve (Shadows/Darks/Lights/Highlights + 3 split points): toneequal's 'simple' EV-band sliders looked like the ideal match (confirmed real dt_bauhaus_slider_from_params-bound sliders, not a curve widget) but a from-scratch investigation reading darktable's actual C source (src/iop/toneequal.c) found the value-changed callback for those sliders never invokes dt_dev_add_history_item -- confirmed empirically across many angles (correct widget order, page-then-values, expanding the module panel first, waiting well past any debounce, forcing enable in isolation, testing against completely fresh images with zero prior history to rule out stale-data artifacts): the slider visibly updates but nothing ever commits to darktable's history table. filmicrgb's contrast/latitude/balance sliders were tried next on the same theory (also confirmed genuine dt_bauhaus_slider_from_params bindings) and hit the exact same dead end. Both failing modules have one thing in common that every working module doesn't: they're already enabled by darktable's own auto-applied default workflow (enable query returns 1 before any interaction), versus every module we successfully drive being off by default. This looks like updating an already-auto-applied module's params follows a different, Lua-unreachable code path -- not confirmed as the root cause, just the strongest available signal, and not worth chasing further given two independent modules already hit the identical wall. Fallback: blend Shadows2012+ParametricShadows+0.5*ParametricDarks into shadhi's 'shadows' slider, and Highlights2012+ParametricHighlights+0.5*ParametricLights into its 'highlights' slider (Darks/Lights get half weight since they're not shadhi's primary zone). Coarser than a real 4-zone system, but shadhi is proven to commit reliably.
colorgrade_note: ColorGrade* (colorbalancergb's 4-way wheels: shadow/midtone/highlight/global hue+chroma+luminance) are NOT graphical-only widgets, contrary to an earlier assumption -- reading colorbalancergb.c's gui_init found they're genuine dt_bauhaus_slider_from_params sliders, same as everything else that works in this project. The real paths (found via source, not guessed): sections 'offset'/'lift'/'gain'/'power' (global/shadows/midtones/highlights respectively) each with 'hue'/'chroma'/'luminance' sliders, e.g. iop/colorbalancergb/lift/hue -- confirmed dt.gui.action resolves every one of these 12 paths (real, non-nan values), both with plain value/set and with the up/down nudge trick that made colorzones work. CONFIRMED DEAD END anyway: verified via byte-level comparison of the actual committed op_params blob (not just the call's return value, which had burned us on toneequal/filmicrgb) that NEITHER approach changes a single byte of what darktable actually saves, tested on the same image proven reliable all session (ruling out stale/fresh-image artifacts). The difference from colorzones: colorzones' curve is a custom-drawn graph widget with its own working commit path; colorbalancergb's '4 ways' page is a plain notebook tab of ordinary sliders that are simply not the module's default/master page -- same category of dead end as toneequal and filmicrgb. The module's actual default page ('master': global saturation/chroma/vibrance/contrast) works fine, which is why ACR's plain Saturation is already mapped there.
unmapped_reason: ColorGrade* -- see colorgrade_note above; a confirmed dead end, not merely unmapped. SplitToning*'s shadow/highlight hue+saturation are graphical color-picker widgets, not plain sliders -- only splittoning's plain 'balance' slider resolved. Texture/Whites2012/Blacks2012 have no comparable darktable widget at all.
